content:
Thank you for your screen shot which looks like the third one of my collection. As a doctor would say "your picture is pathognomonic for a corrupt prefs.js file"... PC or Thunderbird crashes or power outage can damage prefs.js which is one of the most important files in the Thunderbird profile since it contains, among other data, all account parameters. When this happens Thunderbird renames the prefs.js file in prefs-.js (or invalidprefs,js) and creates a new virgin prefs,js file with a size of 6 to 7 kB which doesn't contain any account parameters.

In the Thunderbird menu bar go to Help > Troubleshooting Information > Profile Folder > Open Folder, then quit Thunderbird. The contents of the profile folder is now displayed in an Explorer window: to confirm the diagnostic search for a prefs.js file with a size of 6 or 7 kB and a prefs-1 (or prefs-x.js) file with an actual time stamp and a size of several dozen kB. If you have a backup copy of your Thunderbird profile folder make a copy of the prefs.js file and replace the actual virgin prefs.js with the copy. Then restart Thunderbird.

Open the Thunderbird profile folder via Help > Troubleshooting Information > Profile Folder > Open Folder, then quit Thunderbird. The recently created profile folder "xxxxxxxx.esr" is now displayed in Windows Explorer. Move one level up in the folder hierarchy to open the folder "Profiles". Now open the Thunderbird profile manager: press the Windows Key + R on the keyboard. A Run dialog will open. In the Run dialogue box type: thunderbird -P https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profile-manager-create-and-remove-thunderbird-profiles#w_start-the-profile-manager-when-thunderbird-is-closed

The little profile manager window will open: select your old profile and hit "Start Thunderbird". Thunderbird should open your old profile with your accounts, folders, messages, address books, calendars, ...etc.

content:
- Is this an IMAP or POP3 account?

- Are the "missing" messages visible when you look in SaskTel's webmail interface?

- Might they be in the Trash folder?

- Can you use the Global Search to look for a known missing email to see if it might have accidentally been moved to another folder?

- Is it possible that you've run out of storage space on their servers? (see <https://support.sasktel.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/11342/~/understanding-your-sasktel.net-storage-limit-and-usage>)

If this is an IMAP account, settings in Thunderbird that might affect this would include

- The default setting for the entire account is found at <Account Settings | (account) | Synchronization & Storage | Disk Space> where you can set it automatically remove messages that are older than [x] days (the default is "Synchronize all messages locally regardless of age".)

You can also override the default per folder by right-clicking on the folder name in the Folders List and choosing <Properties" | Retention Policy tab>

It's possible to delete messages according to date or age with the use of Message Filters, but you have to make the effort set the filter up. I'm assuming you would know if you had done that.

I hope we can help you find your missing messages, but consider this a reminder that you should make regular backups of your Thunderbird Profile if your email store is valuable to you.

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/thunderbird-export

p.s. - I doubt this has anything to do with the Microsoft outage, though if your messages were stored on their servers as with an IMAP account, it's remotely possible they could have lost them. There's no way we can know unless they were to tell you.
